 Order

This petition is filed by accused Nos.1 to 3 under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. for quashing the criminal proceedings in C.C.No.17376/2020 pending on the file of XXX Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Court, Bengaluru, arising out of Crime No.105/2020 registered by the Subramanyapura Police Station and charge sheeted for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 448, 323, 506 read with Section 34 of IPC.
2.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Heard the learned counsel for petitioners, learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent No.1- State and learned counsel for respondent No.2.
3.

The case of the prosecution is that the complainant-respondent No.2 who is the wife of the petitioner No.1 filed complaint to the Police on 14.06.2020 alleging that she was married to petitioner No.1 on 08.02.2019 at the Sub-Registrar Office and he was working at Hospete.

Subsequently she stayed with him at Hospete, during her stay with accused No.1, she found accused was chronic drunker and ill-tempered, chain smoker and when she was pregnant, accused No.1 constantly abused her emotionally and also abused her physically and during that time, most of the months, she was forced to pay the rent and house hold medical expenditure.

Accused No.1 was not maintaining her, she wanted to come to maternal home for delivery but at the instance of accused No.1, she went to house of the accused No.2 at Bengaluru and due to lock down, she could not come to Bengaluru.
Later, with the help of her father she came to Bangalore during the lockdown.

sentences.text: she gave birth to a child, but the petitioners did not visit the house to see the child and the accused No.1 continuously troubled her and he was emotionally blackmailing her through messages after drinking alcohol.
She further alleges that she has blocked the whatsapp messages and emotionally broke down and there were irrevocable differences between them.

On the day of the complaint,
accused Nos.2 and 3 came to the father's house to the apartment and they abused her in filthy language, they tried to snatch the child from her and created nuisance in the apartment.
She also scared by their suicidal threats.
Therefore, prayed for taking action.
After registering the case, the Police investigated the matter and filed the charge sheet which is under challenge.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioners has contended that there is no ingredient to attract Sections 498A, 323 and 506 of IPC.
The respondent No.2 herself filed a complaint and also a case under the D.V. Act before the Magistrate apart from divorce case.
Absolutely, there is no statement of any of the witnesses recorded from neighbour of the apartment nor the security guard to show that the incident was held on 13.06.2020.
The petitioners cannot go to the apartment, there will be security and there is no medical record, to show these petitioners were assaulted the complainant.
The legal proceedings, divorce case is pending in the Family Court.
The complaint is filed to harass the petitioner as it was a love marriage, hence prayed for allowing the petition.

5. Per contra, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has objected the petition and contended that the petitioners are continuously abused the respondent physically and mentally and without going to the trial, the Court cannot quash the FIR or charge sheet.
Hence, prayed for dismissing the petition.
6. The learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent No.1 also argued the same.

7. Having heard the arguments, perused the records, on perusal of the same, the statement of the complainant, her father and so many others witnesses were examined by the Investigation Officer in order to show that the accused No.1 abused her physically and mentally and he was not taken care of the complainant after their marriage that too when she was pregnant while staying at Hospete.
The petitioner forced to pay the house rent, medical expenditure and house hold expenditures when she wants to come to Bangalore.
Accused No.1 insisted her to go to her mother's house at Mangaluru and even at Mangaluru, the accused did not taken care of her when she was crying.
However, she has managed to come to Bengaluru and stayed with her parents house.

After she gave birth to child,
the accused No.1 not chosen to visit and see the child, rather he used to abuse her in filthy language and sending whatsapp messages.
He was also addicted to alcohol and continuously harassing the complainant.

The statement of her father, one of the parents and one of her friend apart from brother were all stated that the accused harassing the complainant and she used to intimate the same to the friends and relatives.
All the statements were recorded by Investigation Officer during the investigation.
It is not in dispute that the petitioner No.1 married respondent No.2, which is a love marriage.
Thereafter, he has not taken care of her and harassing her physically and mentally.
Therefore, it cannot be said that there is no ingredient to attract Section 498A of IPC.

However, as regards to the incident dated 13.06.2020, accused Nos.2 and 3 said to have come to Bengaluru to see the child and the complainant has stated the accused tried to snatch the child, of course, there is no statement of the neighbor witnesses and security guard statements were recorded by the Mr. Sanjay Daniel vs The State Of Karnataka

3 Investigating Officers
There is no medical documents to show accused Nos.2 and 3 assaulted the complainant with hand.

Therefore, on prima facie going to the allegation, which appears to be vague and if accused Nos.2 and 3 came to the house of the complainant which is daughter-in-law's house to see the child, that cannot be considered as trespass and attempt to assault her in order to attract Sections 323 and 448 of IPC.
They could have come for seeing the grand child and it cannot be said it is an offence committed by the accused Nos.2 and 3.
However, there is an ample evidence available against accused No.1 for going to the trial and absolutely there is no material to frame the charges against accused Nos.2 and 3.
Therefore, I am of the view the petitioner Nos.2 and 3 have made out case for quashing the charge sheet.

8. Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following order:
The petition is allowed in part.
The petition filed by petitioner No.1 is dismissed.
The proceedings against accused Nos.2 and 3 in C.C.No.17376/2020 pending on the file of the XXX Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Court, Bengaluru is hereby quashed.
